title: UnitedHealthcare Pays Pharmacists to Do More. Bird Flu Hits the Top Egg Producer. Anthropic Debuts Today.
subject: UnitedHealthcare Pays Pharmacists to Do More. Bird Flu Hits the Top Egg Producer. Anthropic Debuts Today.
preview_text: Your pharmacist may do more checkups, bird flu idles a Florida egg farm, and Anthropic starts trading.
description: UnitedHealthcare expands a program paying local pharmacists for medical services, Cal-Maine culls 1.8 million birds, and Anthropic begins trading after a record IPO.
contents_extra: What Anthropic's record IPO means for markets, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Your Local Pharmacist Could Soon Handle More of Your Checkups

photo.alt: Pharmacy storefront with a street sign; file photo.

paragraphs: UnitedHealth Group said Wednesday it plans to expand a program that pays independent pharmacists for medical services, Reuters reports. Those services are normally provided in doctors' offices. The insurer pays pharmacists in a national network, subject to state laws.

The company says the model covers flu and strep testing, diabetes and blood pressure support, and medication counseling. It is now open to Community Plan members in seven states, including Florida and Michigan. The insurer says it plans to add more states.

stories.title: Bird Flu Forces the Biggest US Egg Producer to Cull 1.8 Million Birds

photo.alt: Brown eggs in a cardboard tray; file photo.

paragraphs: Cal-Maine Foods said Wednesday it will cull about 1.8 million birds after bird flu was found at a Florida facility, CNBC reports. That is 2.7% of its flock. The company has halted production at the site.

Al Jazeera reports eggs average $2.32 a dozen, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, far below the record $6.23 in 2025. About 21.5 million birds have been affected this year. Health officials say the risk to the public remains low.

stories.title: Europe Offers Ukraine a New Loan It Repays Only If Russia Pays

photo.alt: European Union flag outside a brick building; file photo.

paragraphs: The European Commission proposed up to EUR 45 billion in new support for Ukraine in 2027 on Wednesday. That would cover about two-thirds of an estimated EUR 70 billion gap. Ukraine would repay the principal only after receiving Russian reparations.

Reuters reports Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Ukraine would only need to repay after Russia paid for war damage. The Commission says up to EUR 25 billion would go to military help. Budget aid would depend on anti-corruption reforms.

stories.title: Voyager 1 Is Now About a Full Light-Day Away From Earth

photo.alt: Large radio dishes against a night sky; file photo.

paragraphs: NASA calculated that Voyager 1 would reach one light-day from Earth on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. EST. That is the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 16 billion miles. No other human-made object has gone that far.

Reuters reports the milestone is based on advance computations by NASA, so the probe is believed to have reached it. Voyager 1 launched in 1977. NASA says its twin, Voyager 2, should reach the same distance in November 2035.

deep_dive.title: Anthropic Begins Trading After the Biggest IPO on Record

photo.alt: Market data screen seen through glass; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on Wednesday, above its expected range, CNBC reports. It sold about 980 million shares and raised $81.3 billion. That tops SpaceX's record June offering. The Claude maker begins trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the new ticker symbol ANT.

Why it matters. The AP reports the price values Anthropic at $1.5 trillion. Shares were set to debut sometime after the market opened at 9:30 a.m. EST. Employees will be able to sell vested stock. The AP cites worries about a possible regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year.

What each side says. The pricing is "a big win for the tech sector," Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said, according to the AP. The AP notes Anthropic has $6.2 billion in debt and is unprofitable under standard accounting rules. The company says it has deals requiring $900 billion in spending on computing and infrastructure.

What comes next. CNBC reported that perpetual futures indicated a 25% pop at the open, as of 10:30 a.m. ET. The Nasdaq was up 0.6% and the S&P 500 0.1%. Alphabet rose almost 3% and Amazon under 1%. Both have invested in Anthropic. Plancorp strategist Callie Cox cautioned that hot IPOs rarely perform well right out of the gate.

World view: Trump, Xi and Putin hold three-way talks. They discussed Ukraine and nuclear arms control in Shenzhen but made no immediate statements; Reuters reports.
Ethiopia and Eritrea mass troops on their border. Conflict monitors and people tied to Tigray militias say the build-up raises fears of war; Reuters reports.
Bangladesh deploys paramilitary troops. Unrest has grown over former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's planned return from exile in December; Reuters reports.
Israel's parliament picks a new speaker. Lawmakers backed by Netanyahu opponents elected Matan Kahana by 66 votes to 52; Reuters reports.
Need to know: Hackers hit popular websites through one tool. A researcher says sites of Zoom, HSBC and Ikea were compromised to steal crypto and target iPhones; Reuters reports.
A plotter against Trump gets 27 years. The DOJ says Asif Merchant of Pakistan was sentenced for a 2024 plot at the behest of Iran; Reuters reports.
House Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker. He won a closed-door vote 251 to 11, according to two sources in the room; NBC News reports.
Pennsylvania confirms an eighth measles death. The state says the person was an unvaccinated resident of Clinton County; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Tech leads stocks midmorning. As of 10:30 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq was up 0.6% while the Dow lost 278 points, or 0.6%; CNBC reports.
Walmart tops estimates and raises its outlook. It earned 65 cents a share adjusted on revenue of $188.84 billion, beating forecasts; CNBC reports.
Walmart online sales jump 17%. The retailer now sees full-year net sales rising 4.9% to 5.2%, up from 4% to 5%; CNBC reports.
Weight-loss drugs cut UK grocery bills. Worldpanel says households with a GLP-1 user spent over 1 billion pounds less than expected; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: The FDA approves a first drug for a rare disorder. Sanofi's pill treats type 3 Gaucher disease, which affects the brain and nervous system; Reuters reports.
An old human species lived in rainforests. Eight fossil teeth from two caves in southern China show Homo erectus lived in rainforest habitat; Reuters reports.
A Spanish rocket firm lands its first client. PLD Space will launch a small Mitsubishi Electric satellite on its MIURA 5 rocket; Reuters reports.
Pfizer licenses Chinese cell therapies. The deal with Starna Therapeutics for three autoimmune CAR-T therapies is worth up to $2.6 billion; Reuters reports.
The score: Alcaraz reaches the ATP Finals semifinals. He beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2 6-4 for his 11th straight win; Reuters reports.
Ash Barty heads to the Hall of Fame. The three-time Grand Slam champion will be inducted in Newport next August; Reuters reports.
Philadelphia gets four more Army-Navy games. The city will host in 2028, 2030, 2032 and 2034 at Lincoln Financial Field; Reuters reports.
LeBron James sues a betting app. He says the app Bron used his nickname and an AI-generated likeness without permission; Reuters reports.
Life & culture: Gordon Ramsay gets a Walk of Fame star. The British chef joked he will polish it every Saturday at 9 a.m.; Reuters reports.
Glastonbury names its 2027 headliners. Harry Styles, Sam Fender, Billie Eilish and Cher will top the bill as the festival returns; Reuters reports.
Take-Two shares rose after the GTA VI launch. The stock surged more than 6% Wednesday after the long-awaited game's release; CNBC reports.
Spain's High Court opens a Julio Iglesias probe. Court records show a judge opened a criminal investigation after a complaint by two former employees; Reuters reports.

trivia.question: In what year did Voyager 1 launch?
trivia.explanation: B. 1977. Reuters reports the probe launched in 1977 and is now about 16 billion miles from Earth.
